en.title: NVIDIA reports record revenue and confirms Vera Rubin volume production
en.coreFact: NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 revenue was $96.22B, +106% YoY; data center revenue was $89B, +117%; Q3 guide is $108B (±2%); Vera Rubin is in full production and expected to be ~20% of Q3 data center revenue; CFO sees ~70% FY2028 revenue growth; management frames opportunity as ~$400B revenue per 1GW of compute deployed.

en.title: US July PCE at 3.7% forces market to reprice rate-hike risk
en.coreFact: July PCE rose 3.7% YoY vs 3.6% expected; core PCE was 3.3%; the federal funds rate is 3.50%-3.75%; the market now sees a slightly higher chance of a Fed hike; the 10Y Treasury yield is about 4.64%; the 2s/30s curve closed at its flattest since the July FOMC; Boston Fed's Collins supports holding rates only if inflation keeps falling.
en.whyItMatters: Higher-for-longer or a hike raises debt financing costs for AI infrastructure just as Anthropic, OpenAI, SoftBank and others are adding billions in leverage, exposing the AI boom's growing dependence on cheap capital.

zh.title: 美国7月PCE同比3.7%超预期，市场重新定价加息风险

en.title: Anthropic signs $45B, six-year compute lease with Nscale using on-site gas power
en.coreFact: Anthropic will pay Nscale $45B over six years for ~460MW at the Monarch site in West Virginia; the system begins ramping in late 2027 using Nvidia Vera Rubin; Nscale's Phase 1 plans 1.35GW with a long-term power runway of over 8GW and a target of 2GW from Caterpillar gas microgrid generation by early 2028; Nscale also has a 1.35GW LOI with Microsoft and closed $790M project financing for its Narvik, Norway data center.
en.whyItMatters: This is the largest known single AI compute lease and brings natural-gas on-site generation into hyperscale AI, shifting the energy strategy debate beyond nuclear and grid extension. It also entrenches the 'neocloud' model and a cross-Atlantic AI infrastructure structure.
en.processMatchReason: No existing process in the dossier fits this compute-lease-plus-energy signal; suggestedProcessId is null.

en.title: Taiwan indicts nine, including an Nvidia employee, for smuggling B300 servers to China
en.coreFact: Keelung prosecutors indicted nine people including a Taiwan-based Nvidia employee; 130 high-end AI servers with B300 chips were allegedly exported through Japan and Indonesia to evade US controls; 74 reached China and 56 were seized; a Super Micro employee and Taiwanese distributors were named; prosecutors seek up to 5 years for four people; B300 chips built at TSMC Phoenix are then packaged in Taiwan.
en.whyItMatters: US export-control enforcement has moved down to individuals, logistics and packaging, operated by Taiwan's judiciary. The Taiwan packaging step is a physical chokepoint in the allied AI supply chain, now shown to be vulnerable to insider smuggling.

en.title: Texas ERCOT audit finds ~474GW of interconnection requests, 90% from data centers
en.coreFact: Governor Abbott ordered a suspension of data center interconnection progress; PUCT and ERCOT are auditing the queue of ~250-300 projects; ERCOT disclosed it is considering ~474GW of interconnection requests, ~90% of which are data centers; large-load reports were deferred. en.whyItMatters: Grid interconnection approval is becoming the physical ceiling on compute expansion. Texas's administrative pause may push capital to other states and strengthen the model of co-locating generation with compute, as in the Nscale deal.

sources.title: Nscale Monarch details and Microsoft LOI

analysis.rationale: The Anthropic-Nscale $45B six-year compute lease (~460MW at Monarch, West Virginia, ramping late 2027 on Vera Rubin; Phase 1 at 1.35GW with >8GW runway; 2GW Caterpillar gas microgrid target by early 2028; plus 1.35GW Microsoft LOI and $790M Narvik financing) is the single most structurally revealing item in this cycle. It (1) is the largest known single AI compute lease, (2) introduces on-site natural-gas generation directly into hyperscale AI, shifting the energy debate beyond nuclear and grid extension, and (3) entrenches the 'neocloud' / lease-rather-than-own model. It fuses the AI-infrastructure-race and energy-security processes and elevates a new structural hypothesis: AI capacity is increasingly financed and provisioned through third-party compute leases co-located with dedicated (including fossil-gas) generation, decoupling compute growth from grid interconnection. Evidence is strong (Bloomberg, Reuters primary-led) with meaningful corroboration. This is today's Global Insight.
warnings: Bloomberg/Reuters are paywalled and details (e.g., site specifics) need direct confirmation
Gas microgrid reliance introduces ESG/political friction not yet surfaced in the sources
Nscale's 8GW+ pipeline is an aspiration; current confirmed near-term capacity (~460MW committed + 1.35GW phase) should not be conflated

It is a close runner-up, but as a policy/regulatory development it is better characterized as reinforcing the AI Infrastructure Race process rather than launching a distinct structural hypothesis, and it does not exceed candidate-003's direct evidence of a new provisioning/generation model.
warnings: ~474GW is 'considering' not approved; audit outcome and final queue size unresolved
Regulatory signals are cross-jurisdictional and heterogeneous, requiring care in generalization
No confirmed capital-reallocation effect yet, only the inference that capital shifts elsewhere

en.title: US July PCE at 3.7% forces market to reprice rate-hike risk
en.coreFact: July PCE rose 3.7% YoY vs 3.6% expected; core PCE was 3.3%; the federal funds rate is 3.50%-3.75%; the market now sees a slightly higher chance of a Fed hike; the 10Y Treasury yield is about 4.64%; the 2s/30s curve closed at its flattest since the July FOMC; Boston Fed's Collins supports holding rates only if inflation keeps falling.
en.whyItMatters: Higher-for-longer or a hike raises debt financing costs for AI infrastructure just as Anthropic, OpenAI, SoftBank and others are adding billions in leverage, exposing the AI boom's growing dependence on cheap capital.
en.processMatchReason: No existing process in the dossier fits this macro-financial repricing signal; suggestedProcessId is null.

analysis.rationale: US July PCE at 3.7% YoY (vs 3.6% expected), core 3.3%, and market repricing toward a possible Fed hike are macroeconomically significant, especially given 10Y yields around 4.64% and a flattening curve. The relevant cross-link is that a higher-for-longer or hiking regime raises debt costs precisely as AI investors (Anthropic, OpenAI, SoftBank) add leverage, exposing the AI boom's dependence on cheap capital. But the signal is preliminary (one-month miss, 'slightly higher chance' of hike), and its chain to AI infrastructure is a second-order risk thesis rather than an established causal process. It is important now but premature to convert into a long-running process; it does not beat candidate-003 or candidate-005 for the single Global Insight.
warnings: A single 0.1pp PCE miss is thin evidence for a policy-regime reversal
The link to AI infrastructure financing is inferential, not yet demonstrated in data
Boston Fed's Collins comments actually support holding, softening the hike signal
